reading.body:
Six interactive estimators cover the questions that decide whether an AI project is viable: token cost, GPU memory, context window fit, training cost, energy and carbon, and return on investment.

The set is a decision layer, not a measurement layer. Each tool shows its own arithmetic and states what it excludes, which means the output is only as good as the inputs a user supplies. The six questions map to distinct constraints: memory and context window are hardware limits, token and training cost are money limits, energy and carbon are power limits, and return on investment is the business limit that decides whether any of the others get funded.

For AI specifically, the pairing of GPU memory and context window with energy and carbon is the useful part. Those four sit on the same physical chain, since memory capacity and context length are set by the accelerators, and the accelerators are set by the power and cooling a building can deliver. A viability estimate that treats model choice as free and power as external will understate the constraint that actually binds.

What the data does not contain is any calculator output, any worked example, or any stated input range. It names six tools and their coverage, and nothing about their accuracy or the assumptions behind their formulas. A reader cannot tell from this whether the estimates agree with measured costs, only that the tools exist and declare their exclusions.
